clue.text: One fabric or another used in church

indicators.note: one piece is used inside the other, so the church letters wrap round the second fabric

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
rep is another fabric, a ribbed cloth

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a material, or a second one, for the church furnishings.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a thin crinkled cloth, so it is one kind of textile.

clue.text: Old coach making, daily, a stop at clubs

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day
to ban is to stop
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: An old coach on a daily run that calls at clubs along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc was an early open motor coach used for outings, now long out of service.

clue.text: Incitement to rebellion abandoned by / second printing of paper

indicators.note: the word for incitement is left behind by the letter for second, which drops out

parts.note: sedition is incitement to rebellion

explanation.surface: A rebellious newspaper is dropped when a second print run appears.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash in the clue is an artefact of the printed page and does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one printing or issue of a newspaper.

clue.text: Discharge mud out of motorway into river

indicators.note: the trimmed mud goes into the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: the motorway letter comes out of the word mud

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Mud from a motorway is discharged into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes M from MUD, leaving UD, which goes 'into' EXE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exude is to ooze out or emit, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: They hold police court responsible for splitting damages

indicators.note: the court word splits the damages word in two by sitting inside it

parts.note: scars as a verb means damages or marks
a quad is a quadrangle, a college court

explanation.surface: A court held responsible for causing damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'responsible for' is only a link; 'court' is a college quadrangle, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Squad cars are police patrol vehicles, which carry officers.

clue.text: Quiet time in airport will be soon

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: the time letter sits inside the airport's name

parts.note: Orly is a Paris airport

explanation.surface: A lull at the airport will come before long.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortly means in a little while, a synonym of soon.

clue.text: Free from restraint, run past wildly

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of run past are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A creature freed from its harness runs past wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To unstrap is to undo the straps holding something, releasing it.

clue.text: Cleaner to do for the clergy

parts.note: to dish, in British slang, is to ruin or do for someone
the cloth means the clergy as a body

explanation.surface: A cleaner who does for the local vicars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do for' also means to clean house for someone, which makes 'Cleaner' look like a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishcloth is a cloth for washing dishes, so a cleaning item.

clue.text: Drink Mark imported just right for consumption

indicators.note: the drink takes in the mark word, bringing it inside

parts.note: ale is a drink
a dent is a mark

explanation.surface: An imported beer bearing a brand mark that is just right to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Al dente describes pasta cooked to be firm to the bite, correctly done for eating.

clue.text: Fire missiles at boat

explanation.definitionFit: Shelling is artillery bombardment, and a shell is also a narrow racing craft.

clue.text: Claudius poorly, having swallowed old tart

indicators.note: the rearranged emperor takes the letter for old inside
poorly signals that the letters of the name are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: The emperor Claudius is unwell after eating an old pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' makes ACIDULUS from CLAUDIUS; 'having swallowed' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidulous means sour-tasting, a synonym of the adjective tart.

clue.text: Grass forming southern border

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: Grass growing along the southern edge of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like marsh plant, loosely classed as grass.

clue.text: Down which vital supplies sail?

parts.note: a waterway carrying food is the surface; the real channel is the gut, through which nourishment passes

explanation.surface: Barges carry essential cargo down a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: This digestive tract is the passage food travels through, and its name sounds like a nourishing waterway.

clue.text: Pardon little woman defending home

indicators.note: the woman's name surrounds and so guards the home word

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Little Women
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A forgiving woman protects her household.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's novel; Amy is the youngest sister.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is a general pardon granted by a government.

clue.text: Stage in race is transformed into a mockery

indicators.note: the stage word goes in the middle of the rearranged letters
transformed says the letters of race and is change shape

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a race or journey

explanation.surface: A leg of a race is turned into a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' makes SACRIE from RACE IS; LEG goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilege is profanation of something holy, treating it with mocking disrespect.

clue.text: Saw artistic group about deliveries

indicators.note: the group's letters go about, wrapping round, the deliveries word

parts.note: PRB is the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, a Victorian group of painters
an over in cricket is a set of six deliveries

explanation.surface: A painter's circle saw something about deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is a noun, an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying or maxim, the same as an adage.

clue.text: One stops hitting drum when you put your foot down

definitions.text: One stops hitting drum when you put your foot down

parts.words: One stops hitting drum when you put your foot down
parts.note: reads like a drummer told to stop; really it is the vehicle part that presses on the brake drum when the pedal is pressed

explanation.surface: A drummer is told to stop when someone puts their foot down.
explanation.definitionFit: This part is the curved block that presses against a wheel's drum to slow a vehicle.

clue.text: Colt and bucking bronco given part of 23

indicators.note: a bucking horse throws itself about, so the letters of bronco are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A young horse and a wild bronco are given some feed.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncob is the central core of an ear of corn, part of the 23-across plant.

clue.text: Crumbs! Mother's in control

indicators.note: the mother word goes inside the control word

parts.note: reins are a means of control
ma is mother; the 's means is

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that Mother has taken charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs!' looks like an exclamation but is the noun: leftover bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Remains are what is left over, as crumbs are leftovers of food.

clue.text: Looking astonished as computer error's observed

parts.note: a bug is a computer error; the 's is just is
eyed means observed

explanation.surface: A programmer stares in surprise on noticing a software glitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with bulging eyes from surprise is wide-eyed with amazement.

clue.text: Difficulty communicating from Continent with Herbert

parts.note: A P H is A.P. Herbert, humorist and MP
Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: Someone from abroad, travelling with Herbert, struggles to make themself understood.
explanation.walkthrough: A.P. Herbert was a British humorist known by his initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphasia is loss of the ability to use or understand language, usually after brain damage.

clue.text: Validly executed, in gruesome manner

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the first letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: lawfully means validly

explanation.surface: A properly carried out execution, done horribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' looks like 'carried out' but means beheaded: LAWFULLY loses L.
explanation.definitionFit: Awfully means dreadfully or horribly, in a gruesome way.

clue.text: Son in possession of what Esau was deprived of?

parts.note: having means in possession of

explanation.surface: A son who owns what Esau lost, his birthright.
explanation.walkthrough: Esau, Jacob's brother in Genesis, was a hairy man and lost his birthright; here what he lacked is a razor's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaving is removal of hair with a razor, something hairy Esau never had.

clue.text: Bound to depart from here?

parts.note: bound reads as destined, but it is a leap; a launching spot is literally a place to leap from

explanation.surface: A traveller certain to set off from this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means a starting point for an enterprise or journey.

clue.text: What confirmed bachelor becomes in Leap Year?

definitions.text: What confirmed bachelor becomes in Leap Year?

parts.words: What confirmed bachelor becomes in Leap Year?
parts.note: by tradition women may propose in a leap year, so an unmarried man grows nervous; leap also suggests springing about

explanation.surface: A single man dreads the year when women can propose.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpy means nervous and on edge, as a wary single man would be.

clue.text: Call to sharpen up putting pressure on

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen

explanation.surface: A call to sharpen up a performance under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the P is put 'on' top of HONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To phone is to call someone by telephone.

clue.text: Puzzling place in which to find one US crop

indicators.note: the single letter is found inside the puzzling place

parts.note: a maze is a puzzling place
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Getting lost in a field of crops in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is the cereal grown across the American corn belt.

clue.text: Somewhat sensational, rather like the Sun?

definitions.meaning: the yellow press is sensational journalism, and -ish means somewhat
the sun appears a golden colour; the Sun is also a British tabloid

explanation.definitionFit: The yellow press means lurid newspapers, and a pale golden tint is also like the sun.

clue.text: Occasion of recent jam session?

parts.note: a jam session suggests jazz, but this alludes to the Looking-Glass rule of jam tomorrow and jam the day before, never jam today

explanation.surface: Musicians recall when they last improvised together.
explanation.walkthrough: In Through the Looking-Glass the White Queen offers jam tomorrow and jam on the previous day, but never today.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before today is the most recent past day, when that jam was had.

clue.text: Predator taking head off pack animal

indicators.note: the first letter is removed, like a head lopped off

parts.note: a beagle is a hound that hunts in packs

explanation.surface: A hunter decapitates a beast of burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pack animal' suggests a mule but means a hound in a hunting pack.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a bird of prey, a hunter of other animals.
